# Irreducibility after reduction of an admissible sl2 lattice

## Original exercise

James E. Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*,
Graduate Texts in Mathematics 9, Springer, section 27, exercise 7,
printed page 164. The exercise-list convention on page 163 sets
\(L=\mathfrak{sl}_2\) and identifies weights with integers.
Book DOI: [10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2).

> 7. If \(0\leq\lambda<\operatorname{char}K\), \(V=V(\lambda)\),
> prove that \(V(K)\) is irreducible as \(L(K)\)-module.

## Definitions and complete target

Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.
conclusion: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W⊆V_K, if W is invariant under the induced x,y,h then W={0} or W=V_K. Equivalently V(K) is irreducible as an L(K)-module. This holds for every given prime p, field K of characteristic p, integer 0≤λ<p, and arbitrary admissible lattice M, including λ=0 and p=2, without assuming K algebraically closed.

hypotheses.statement: p is a prime number and K has characteristic p.

V is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂(ℂ)-module of highest weight λ, of complex dimension λ+1. The Chevalley generators x,y,h of sl₂(ℂ) act on V and satisfy [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=−2y, [x,y]=h. In its universal enveloping algebra and in the induced operators on V, the bracket is [a,b]=ab−ba; the same symbols denote the corresponding operators.
v∈V is nonzero, xv=0, and hv=λv.
M⊂V is an arbitrary admissible lattice: a free abelian subgroup admitting an integer basis which is also a complex basis of V, and stable under U_Z. No minimal-lattice assumption is imposed.

definitions.type: positive integer viewed as a natural number

definitions.definition: I={i∈ℤ:0≤i≤λ}; indices of finite sums over I are expression-bound.

definitions.type: family of elements of U(sl₂(ℂ)), also denoting their complex-linear actions on V
definitions.definition: For every natural number r, X_r=x^r/r! in U(sl₂(ℂ)), also denoting its induced operator on V. The zeroth power is the enveloping algebra identity, acting as Id_V.

definitions.type: family of elements of U(sl₂(ℂ)), also denoting their complex-linear actions on V
definitions.definition: For every natural number r, Y_r=y^r/r! in U(sl₂(ℂ)), also denoting its induced operator on V. The zeroth power is the enveloping algebra identity, acting as Id_V.

definitions.type: unital integer subalgebra of the universal enveloping algebra acting on V
definitions.definition: U_Z is the unital ℤ-subalgebra of U(sl₂(ℂ)) generated by X_r=x^r/r! and Y_r=y^r/r! for all natural numbers r. Its action on V is that induced by x,y,h.

definitions.definition: R=ℤ_(p)={a/b∈ℚ:a,b∈ℤ, b≠0, p∤b}, with its usual subring operations.

definitions.type: R-linear map M_R→V (V restricted to R)
definitions.definition: iota(r⊗m)=rm for r∈R and m∈M; its image is the R-span of M. Identification of M_R with this image is made only after its injectivity is proved.
E_ij is the unique complex-linear map taking e_j to e_i and all e_k with k∈I and k≠j to zero. This construction is used only after (e_i) is proved to be a complex basis.
Pi=Y_λ X_λ. This is the operator denoted P in the supplied proof; Pi avoids confusion with the target proposition ID P.
J=J_0; the index 0 belongs to I since 0≤λ.
V_K=V(K)=M⊗_ℤ K, with x,y,h acting by their induced lattice operators when their preservation of M is established.

L_K=L(K)=(ℤx+ℤy+ℤh)⊗_ℤ K, formed from the abstract Chevalley generators in sl₂(ℂ), with bracket induced by [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=−2y, [x,y]=h. Once preservation of the lattice by these operators is established, its action on V_K is the tensor extension of that lattice action. This is the Chevalley construction also when p=2.

definitions.definition: F_p=ℤ/pℤ, embedded in K by the integer map.
For a/b∈R with p∤b, kappa(a/b)=(a·1_K)(b·1_K)^(-1). Denominators are nonzero since K has characteristic p; cross multiplication makes the expression independent of its representation.
